name: Caul
overview: The term 'caul' in Scripture refers to a specific part of an animal used in sacrificial offerings, most likely the upper lobe of the liver or the midriff above the liver and kidneys. The passages in Exodus and Leviticus consistently describe the caul as being taken along with the fat and kidneys to be burnt on the altar, highlighting its significance in the consecration and atonement rituals. This anatomical detail underscores the careful instructions God gave for offerings, emphasizing the holiness and dedication required in worship.
